query: Consider the following context: How to rationally design composition of alloys with desired properties has always been an open and challenging question, especially for high-entropy alloy (HEA) which has huge selections of composition due to the feature of multi-principal elements. Although great efforts have been made in the past decades, such as approaches based on thermo-kinetic analysis and simulations, strategies to quick determine the optimal HEA composition remain lacking. In that context, which method can be used for design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight refractory HEA (RHEA) compositions, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A machine learning–based inverse design method that integrates high‐throughput computational screening with experimental feedback can rapidly identify RHEA compositions that are simultaneously intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight.
generation.material_initial_state: A broad composition space of multi-principal element refractory alloys with no prior optimization for mechanical performance.
generation.intervention: Application of an inverse design framework that uses machine learning to analyze existing thermo‐kinetic data and simulation outputs, thereby predicting candidate alloy compositions.
generation.conditions: Standard laboratory synthesis and mechanical testing conditions applied to alloys within the refractory element space, with available databases for training the model.
generation.structural_mediator: The microstructural phase stability and defect distributions that result from specific element combinations and concentrations.
generation.mechanism: The machine learning model learns the complex relationships between composition, microstructural evolution, and mechanical properties; it then optimizes alloy compositions to balance high strength with ductility and reduced density by predicting those composition–structure–property correlations.
generation.predicted_outcome: Alloys developed via this ML inverse design method will display significantly improved mechanical performance (higher strength and ductility with lower density) compared to alloys designed solely through traditional thermo‐kinetic simulations or empirical methods.
generation.baseline: RHEA compositions designed with traditional thermo‐kinetic analysis and simulations without integration of data-driven optimization methods.
generation.boundary: The approach may be limited in cases where the training data are sparse or when the refractory elements exhibit extreme segregation behavior or very low mutual solubility, leading to unpredictable microstructures.
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty about the extent to which the machine learning model’s predictions will remain accurate in unexplored regions of the composition space, and whether sufficient high-quality data exist to train a robust model.

falsification_experiment.design: Use the ML inverse design method to select a set of candidate RHEA compositions. Independently, generate a control set of alloys designed via conventional thermo‐kinetic methods. Synthesize both sets and perform standardized mechanical tests (e.g., tensile testing for strength and ductility, density measurements).
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the ML-guided candidates do not statistically and consistently outperform the control alloys in the targeted mechanical properties across multiple experimental replicates, the hypothesis that the ML inverse design method accelerates the discovery of superior RHEAs is falsified.
